newsitem.title: INDIA: Samsung Electronics India to double sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Electronics India to double sales in 1997.

text.p: Samsung India Electronics Ltd, a unit of Korean consumer electronics giant Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, said on Monday its 1997 sales would increase to 4.5 billion rupees ($125.6 million) from 1.38 billion in 1996.

"Our sales should touch 4.5 billion rupees this year, as we expand our network to cover the entire country, and add more products," R.K. Caprihan, deputy managing director, Samsung India told reporters.

He said that over the 12 months, the company had added washing machines, a new line of audio systems, facsimile machines and feature phones. Samsung India launched a range of microwave ovens and still cameras on Monday.

"With our manufacturing facility starting production, we expect our sales to boom," he said. Samsung India will inaugurate its first manufacturing plant in India, capable of making 400,000 colour televisions a year, on Friday, June 27.

Over the next five years, Samsung India plans to start local manufacture of refrigerators, washing machines, air conditoners and microwave ovens. Earlier plans were to start local manufacture of all these products in three years.

Currently, Samsung India sources colour televisions and audio systems from local manufacturers. It imports refrigerators, washing machines, microwave ovens, cameras, facsimile machines and telephones.

Speaking at the news conference, Samsung India's managing director, B.M. Park said: "The local conditions have not been conducive to high growth. The market has not grown as per our expectations. We will now structure our investments over six years instead of three."
He said that Samsung had invested about $25 million in India, with $20 million in a joint venture with Larsen & Toubro Ltd for telecommunications equipment.
It has also invested $5 million in the equity of Samsung India Electronics Ltd (Samsung India), which is 51 percent owned by Samsung Electronics.
Park said Samsung had decided to delay local manufacture of colour picture tubes, parts and components for colour televisions, and audio systems.
